title: Marketing Analytics & Reporting
subtitle: Measure marketing across every channel, reconcile the numbers with real sales, and write reports that lead to clear budget decisions.
description: An advanced, practical course for women who already do digital marketing and want to prove what works. You will build a measurement plan, set up trustworthy GA4 and UTM tracking, reconcile ad platform claims with payment records, and produce a one-page Looker Studio report with checked insights. You finish with a priced analytics offer and a 90-day plan to win clients.
outcomes: Write a measurement plan with exact KPI formulas, baselines, targets and a KPI tree
Explain attribution models and calculate the true effect of ads with a holdout test
Set up GA4 key events and UTM links that land in the correct channel groups
Reconcile Meta, Google Ads, GA4 and payment data into one honest set of figures
Build a one-page Looker Studio report with insights in what, so what, now what format
Price, scope and sell analytics work with an audit, a retainer and a 90-day plan
audience: Women who already run or support digital marketing for a business or clients and want to measure, report and sell analytics confidently.
tools: Smartphone and, ideally, a laptop for spreadsheets and dashboards
A Google account (for GA4, the GA4 demo account, Google Sheets and Looker Studio)
Access to at least one business's ad, website or sales data, or the practice data in this course

modules.title: Foundations: Decisions, KPIs and Attribution
modules.overview: You learn what marketing analytics is for, how to write a measurement plan with exact KPI formulas, and how attribution and incrementality decide which channel earned a sale. By the end you can explain to a client why platform numbers disagree and what the business should actually measure.

lessons.title: From activity reports to decisions: what marketing analytics is for
objectives: Explain the difference between reporting activity, reporting performance and reporting business outcomes
Name the four kinds of analytics question: what happened, why, what next, and what to do
Turn a vague request for 'a report' into two or three decision questions
Calculate total marketing spend per order and revenue per naira of marketing spend from simple figures

blocks.text: Many marketing reports in Nigerian businesses look like this: 40 posts this month, 120,000 impressions, 2,300 likes, 3 new ads. The numbers are true, but the owner reading them still cannot answer the question she actually has: **should I keep spending this money, and where?** Marketing analytics is the work of collecting marketing data, checking it, and turning it into answers to business questions like that one.

blocks.name: marketing-analysis
blocks.alt: A person studying marketing charts on a large screen
blocks.caption: Analytics starts with a business question, then looks for the numbers that answer it.

blocks.text: This is an advanced course. It assumes you already run or support some digital marketing (social media, Google or Meta ads, email, WhatsApp, a website or online store) and can use a spreadsheet. Here you learn to measure across all of those channels together, judge which channel truly earned a sale, reconcile numbers that disagree, and write reports that lead to decisions.
Three levels of marketing reporting

head: Level
Example numbers
Question it answers
rows: Posts published, ads launched, emails sent
Did the team do the work?
Click-through rate, cost per click, cost per lead, return on ad spend
Orders, revenue, new customers, qualified leads, cost per order across all marketing
Is marketing growing the business at a cost we can afford?

blocks.text: Activity numbers belong in a report only as context. Channel numbers help the person running each channel improve it. Outcome numbers are what an owner, a manager or a client uses to decide on budget. A strong report moves from the outcome at the top, down to the channels that explain it, and mentions activity only where it explains a change.

blocks.title: What a report should lead with
items: Decision: what to change
Business outcome: sales, leads
Channel efficiency: CPA, ROAS
Activity: posts, impressions
blocks.caption: Read from the top: a report earns its place when the bottom layers explain the decision at the top.

blocks.text: Four kinds of analytics question

items: **Descriptive: what happened?** Revenue from online orders was 1.7 million naira in March.
**Diagnostic: why did it happen?** Orders rose because a new Google search campaign brought buyers who searched for a specific product.
**Predictive: what is likely next?** If the trend holds, April orders should be similar, but the Easter peak may lift them.
**Prescriptive: what should we do?** Move part of the Instagram budget to the search campaign for four weeks and check the result.

blocks.text: Most weak reports stop at descriptive. Your value as an analyst grows each time you move one step further down that list, as long as you are honest about how certain you are. A diagnosis or prediction is a reasoned judgement, so always say what evidence supports it.
Start with the decision, not the data

When a client says "send me a report", ask what she will decide with it. Typical marketing decisions are: how much to spend next month, how to split spend between channels, whether to stop or scale a campaign, which product or offer to promote, and whether a new channel is worth testing. Write each one as a question that a number can answer, for example: "Did each naira spent on Meta ads bring back more than our break-even amount in sales?"

blocks.title: Worked example: rewriting a monthly report around decisions
blocks.context: For example, Amaka runs an online shea butter skincare shop from Lagos. Her assistant sends a monthly report of posts, impressions and likes. Amaka spent 300,000 naira on Meta ads and 150,000 naira on Google ads in March (approximate figures used for practice). Her order sheet shows 95 orders worth 1,710,000 naira.
steps: Ask Amaka her decision: she wants to know if she should raise ad spend in April, and on which platform.
Total marketing spend: 300,000 + 150,000 = 450,000 naira.
Revenue per naira of marketing spend: 1,710,000 / 450,000 = 3.8. Every 1 naira of marketing was matched by 3.80 naira of sales.
Average order value: 1,710,000 / 95 = 18,000 naira. Marketing cost per order: 450,000 / 95 = about 4,737 naira.
Next questions to answer in the report: how much of the 95 orders each platform helped to bring, and whether 4,737 naira per order leaves profit after product cost and delivery.
blocks.result: The new report opens with three outcome numbers (revenue, marketing cost per order, revenue per naira of spend), then breaks them down by channel, and ends with a recommendation for April. Posts and likes move to a short appendix.

blocks.title: Revenue is not profit
blocks.text: A ratio of 3.8 sounds healthy, but whether it is profitable depends on Amaka's gross margin. If product, packaging and delivery cost 60% of the selling price, only 40% of each sale is left to pay for marketing and overheads. Always ask for the margin before calling a result good or bad.
What makes an analyst trusted

items: She checks numbers against money actually received before reporting them.
She shows bad news as clearly as good news.
She says how certain she is, and why.
She ends every report with a specific next step that someone owns.

blocks.text: The rest of this course builds those habits. In the next lesson you will turn a business goal into a small set of key performance indicators with clear formulas and targets.

takeaways: Activity numbers show effort; outcome numbers show results. Lead with outcomes.
Good analytics moves from what happened to why, what next and what to do.
Ask what decision a report must support before you open any dashboard.
Revenue per naira of spend is only meaningful once you know the profit margin.

activity.title: Turn a report request into decision questions
steps: Pick a business you know (your own, a client, a friend's shop) that does some online marketing.
Write down the last marketing report or update they produced, or what they currently look at.
Ask the owner, or imagine, the two biggest marketing decisions they face in the next month.
Rewrite each decision as a question a number can answer.
List the data you would need for each question and where it lives (ad account, website, order book, payment app).
activity.evidence: A one-page note with the two decision questions, the numbers needed and their sources.

lessons.title: Building a measurement plan: objectives, KPI formulas and a KPI tree
objectives: Write a measurement plan that links a business objective to a primary KPI and its driver metrics
Use correct formulas for CTR, CPC, CPM, conversion rate, CPA, ROAS, MER and average order value
Break revenue into sessions, conversion rate and order value to find the cheapest lever
Set targets from a baseline instead of guessing

blocks.text: A **measurement plan** is a short document, often one page, that fixes what you will measure before a campaign or reporting period starts. Writing it first stops two common problems: changing the definition of success after seeing the results, and drowning a client in every number the platforms offer.

blocks.name: metrics
blocks.alt: A person arranging metric cards and charts
blocks.caption: A measurement plan picks a few metrics with clear formulas, not every number available.

blocks.text: The five parts of a measurement plan

items: **Business objective**: the result the business wants, in plain words. Example: grow online fabric sales profitably.
**Primary KPI**: one number that best shows progress on the objective. Example: monthly online revenue, or orders at an acceptable marketing cost per order.
**Driver metrics**: the smaller numbers that move the KPI, such as website sessions, conversion rate and average order value.
**Baselines and targets**: what each number is now, and what you aim for by a date.
**Segments**: the groups you will compare, for example channel, campaign, new versus returning customers, phone versus computer, Lagos versus other states.

blocks.text: Formulas you must get exactly right

head: Metric
Formula
Plain meaning
rows: Share of people shown the ad who clicked
Cost of showing the ad 1,000 times
Share of visits that ended in the action you want
What each lead, sale or sign-up cost
Revenue credited to ads / Ad spend
Sales per naira of one platform's ad spend
Sales per naira across all marketing together

blocks.text: Notice the difference between ROAS and MER. ROAS uses the revenue that one platform says it caused, so each platform reports its own ROAS. MER uses the business's real total revenue and total marketing spend, so it cannot be inflated by two platforms claiming the same sale. Senior managers usually trust MER and blended cost per order more, while channel managers use ROAS to tune each platform. You will use both.

blocks.title: State the denominator
blocks.text: Conversion rate can be calculated per session, per user or per ad click, and the answers differ. Always write which one you used in the plan, and never compare a per-click rate from an ad platform with a per-session rate from your website analytics.
The KPI tree: finding the lever

For an online shop, revenue can be broken into three drivers: **Revenue = Sessions x Conversion rate x Average order value**. This is called a KPI tree because one number branches into the numbers that produce it. Each branch has its own levers: sessions come from traffic channels, conversion rate from the website, offer and trust, and average order value from pricing and bundles.

blocks.title: From objective to measurable targets
items: Business objective
Primary KPI
Driver metrics
Baseline and target
Segments to compare
blocks.caption: Each step narrows a broad goal into numbers you can track and act on.

blocks.title: Worked example: a KPI tree for an online fabric shop
blocks.context: For example, Halima sells Ankara and lace fabrics online from Kano. Last month her shop had 12,000 sessions, a conversion rate of 1.2% and an average order value of 20,000 naira. She wants 3,000,000 naira of online revenue next month.
steps: Baseline orders: 12,000 x 1.2% = 144 orders.
Baseline revenue: 144 x 20,000 = 2,880,000 naira. The gap to target is 120,000 naira.
Orders needed at the same order value: 3,000,000 / 20,000 = 150 orders, so she needs 6 more orders.
Lever A, more traffic: at 1.2% conversion she needs 150 / 0.012 = 12,500 sessions, which is 500 more, an increase of about 4.2%.
Lever B, better conversion: with the same 12,000 sessions she needs 150 / 12,000 = 1.25% conversion, a rise of 0.05 percentage points.
She compares costs: 500 extra sessions from ads might cost more than adding delivery fees to the product page and a WhatsApp help button, which could lift conversion.
blocks.result: The tree shows that a small conversion improvement or a small traffic increase each closes the gap. Halima's plan sets the KPI (online revenue, target 3,000,000 naira), the drivers with baselines, and tests the cheaper lever first.

blocks.text: Leading and lagging indicators

Revenue is a **lagging** indicator: you only see it after customers buy. Add one or two **leading** indicators that move earlier, such as add-to-cart rate, WhatsApp enquiries per day, or leads booked for a consultation. If leading indicators fall in week one, you can act before the monthly revenue is final.

Keep the plan small: one primary KPI, three to five drivers, and two or three segments. Write the formula and data source next to each metric. That single page becomes the specification for your tracking setup in Module 2 and for every report you produce.

takeaways: A measurement plan fixes objective, KPI, drivers, targets and segments before results arrive.
ROAS is one platform's claim; MER uses real total revenue and total spend.
Revenue = sessions x conversion rate x average order value shows where the lever is.
Always state the denominator of a rate, and set targets from a baseline.

activity.title: Write a one-page measurement plan
steps: Choose a real or practice business and write its marketing objective in one sentence.
Choose one primary KPI and write its formula and data source.
List three to five driver metrics with formulas and current baselines (estimate if needed and label as estimates).
Build a KPI tree for revenue or leads and calculate what each lever would need to change to reach a target.
Name two segments you will compare in every report.
activity.evidence: The one-page measurement plan with formulas, baselines and the KPI tree calculation.

lessons.title: Attribution and incrementality: who really earned the sale
objectives: Explain why several channels can claim the same sale
Share credit for one order under last-click, first-click, linear and position-based rules
Describe the attribution models GA4 offers today
Calculate incremental purchases and cost per incremental purchase from a holdout test

blocks.text: Customers rarely buy after one touch. A woman might see an Instagram ad on Monday, search the brand name on Google on Thursday, and buy after clicking an email on Saturday. Three channels touched that order. **Attribution** is the set of rules that decides how much credit each touch receives.

blocks.name: data-points
blocks.alt: Connected data points on a screen
blocks.caption: Each touchpoint in a customer journey is a data point that may share credit for the sale.

blocks.text: Common attribution rules

items: **Last click**: the final clicked touch gets all the credit.
**First click**: the first touch gets all the credit.
**Linear**: every touch gets an equal share.
**Position-based**: often 40% to the first touch, 40% to the last, and 20% shared across the middle.
**Data-driven**: a statistical model compares journeys that converted with journeys that did not, and shares credit according to how much each touch seems to change the chance of buying.

blocks.title: One customer, three touches
items: Day 1: Instagram ad click
Day 4: Google search click
Day 6: email click
Day 6: order paid
blocks.caption: The same order can be credited to Instagram, Google or email depending on the rule you choose.

blocks.title: Worked example: sharing credit for one order
blocks.context: For example, Bola buys a 60,000 naira bundle from an online home goods store after the three touches shown in the timeline: Instagram ad first, Google search second, email last.
steps: Last click: email gets 60,000 naira; Instagram and Google get 0.
First click: Instagram gets 60,000 naira; the others get 0.
Linear: 60,000 / 3 = 20,000 naira each.
blocks.result: Under last click, email looks like the hero and the Instagram ad looks useless. Under first click the opposite. The real order value never changes; only the story does. Always state which rule a number uses.

blocks.text: What GA4 offers today

Google Analytics 4 (GA4) lets you choose the reporting attribution model in the property's Admin settings. According to Google's help centre, the available models are **data-driven**, **paid and organic last click**, and **Google paid channels last click**. The first-click, linear, time-decay and position-based models were removed from GA4 in November 2023. You can still apply those simpler rules yourself in a spreadsheet when you want to explain attribution to a client, as in the worked example.
Why platforms over-claim

Meta Ads Manager and Google Ads each count conversions using their own rules and time windows, and Meta can count a purchase after someone only viewed an ad without clicking. Neither platform knows about the other. So when Bola's order happens, Meta may count it (she clicked an Instagram ad within its window) and Google Ads may also count it. Add the platforms' reported purchases together and you will often get more purchases than the business actually received. Module 2 shows how to reconcile this.
Incrementality: would the sale have happened anyway?

Attribution shares credit among touches. It does not prove that a touch **caused** the sale. Retargeting ads, which follow people who already visited the shop, often report very high ROAS because they reach people who were going to buy anyway. The way to measure cause is an **incrementality test**, also called a holdout test: randomly split similar customers into a group that sees the ads and a group that does not, then compare purchase rates.

The ads group bought 300 times and the holdout group 250 times. Only the difference, 50 purchases, was caused by the ads. Ads Manager might report a cost per purchase of 250,000 / 300 = about 833 naira, but the **cost per incremental purchase** is 250,000 / 50 = 5,000 naira, six times higher. That is the number that tells you whether retargeting is worth its budget.

blocks.title: Check that the gap is not chance
blocks.text: With small groups, a one-point gap can appear by luck. A two-proportion z-test, available in free online A/B test calculators, is the usual check. For these figures the z value is about 2.2, above the common 1.96 threshold for 95% confidence. With 500 people per group the same rates would not be convincing, so plan group sizes before the test.

In your reports, label every channel figure with its source and rule, for example "Meta purchases (Meta's own attribution)" or "GA4 purchases (paid and organic last click)". When the numbers disagree, show them side by side rather than choosing the most flattering one. A client who understands why two honest numbers differ will trust you more than one who later discovers a hidden gap.

Simple versions of holdout tests are possible for small businesses: pause a campaign in one region while keeping it in a similar region, or run it on alternate weeks, then compare. Keep everything else the same, write down the plan before you start, and treat the result as evidence, not proof.

takeaways: Attribution rules share credit; they do not change the real sale.
GA4 now offers data-driven and last-click models; the others were removed in November 2023.
Ad platforms each claim conversions under their own rules, so their totals often exceed real orders.
Incrementality tests compare exposed and held-out groups to show what ads truly caused.

activity.title: Re-credit five real or practice orders
steps: Write down five orders with their touchpoints in order (ask customers, use UTM data, or invent a labelled practice set).
Give each order its value in naira.
Credit every order under last click, first click, linear and 40/20/40 position-based rules in a spreadsheet.
Total the credit by channel under each rule and check that each rule's total equals the real order total.
Write two sentences on which channel's importance changes most between rules.
activity.evidence: The spreadsheet with four credit columns and the two-sentence conclusion.

quiz.q: A manager's report lists posts made, impressions and likes. What is the most useful first change?
options: Add more social metrics such as saves and shares
Lead with business outcomes such as orders, revenue and marketing cost per order
Remove all numbers and write a narrative instead
Report impressions per post instead of total impressions
quiz.explain: Activity metrics show effort. Owners decide budgets on outcomes, so the report should lead with them and use activity only as context.

quiz.q: Total marketing spend is 400,000 naira and total revenue is 1,400,000 naira. What is the MER?
quiz.explain: MER = total revenue / total marketing spend = 1,400,000 / 400,000 = 3.5.

quiz.q: A shop has 10,000 sessions, 1.5% conversion and an average order value of 15,000 naira. What is revenue?
An order worth 50,000 naira had three touches: Facebook ad, organic search, email. Under 40/20/40 position-based attribution, how much does organic search get?
quiz.explain: The middle touch receives 20% of 50,000, which is 10,000 naira. The first and last touches get 20,000 each.

quiz.q: Retargeting ads went to 4,000 people and 240 bought. A held-out group of 4,000 had 200 purchases. Spend was 200,000 naira. What is the cost per incremental purchase?
quiz.explain: Incremental purchases = 240 - 200 = 40. Cost per incremental purchase = 200,000 / 40 = 5,000 naira.

quiz.q: Which statement about GA4 attribution is correct?
options: GA4 still offers linear and time-decay models
GA4 offers data-driven and last-click models; first click, linear, time decay and position-based were removed in November 2023
GA4 does not allow any attribution setting
quiz.explain: Google's help centre lists data-driven, paid and organic last click, and Google paid channels last click, and says the other four models were removed in November 2023.

modules.title: Tools, Data Pipeline and the Monthly Report
modules.overview: You set up trustworthy tracking in GA4 with UTM links, reconcile ad platform, analytics and payment data into one sheet, and turn it into a one-page Looker Studio report with checked insights. This is the core workflow you will repeat for every client or employer.

lessons.title: Trustworthy tracking: GA4 key events, channel groups and UTM links
objectives: Explain how GA4 records events, key events and the source of each visit
Build UTM-tagged links with the three required parameters and a lowercase naming convention
Choose utm_medium values that land in the correct GA4 default channel group
Set GA4 data retention so explorations can look back far enough

blocks.text: Every report you write is only as good as the tracking under it. In this lesson you set up the website side of marketing measurement with **Google Analytics 4 (GA4)**, Google's free web and app analytics tool, and you learn to tag links so every visit is credited to the right channel.

blocks.name: analytics-setup
blocks.alt: A person setting up an analytics dashboard
blocks.caption: Clean tracking set up once saves hours of guessing in every later report.

blocks.text: Events and key events

GA4 records almost everything as an **event**: a page view, a scroll, a click on a button, a purchase. Some events are collected automatically; others, such as a purchase on an online store, are sent by the shop platform or added by a developer. Google recommends standard names for common actions, for example **purchase**, **generate_lead** and **sign_up**. Using those names helps GA4 reports work as intended.

Events that matter most to the business are marked as **key events** in the Admin area. Older guides and some screens call these conversions. Google now uses "key event" in Analytics and keeps "conversion" for key events used to measure ad campaigns in Google Ads. For a shop the key event is usually purchase; for a service business it may be a form submission or a click on a WhatsApp chat button.

blocks.title: Track the WhatsApp button
blocks.text: Many Nigerian businesses close sales on WhatsApp, so the website shows few purchases. Track clicks on the chat button as an event and mark it as a key event. It is a leading indicator: it shows interest, not payment, so report it separately from orders.
How GA4 decides the channel

For each visit GA4 stores a **source** (where the visitor came from, such as google or instagram) and a **medium** (the type of traffic, such as organic, cpc or email). It then sorts visits into **default channel groups** using fixed rules. A few rules from Google's documentation that matter most:

items: **Email**: source or medium is email (or e-mail, e_mail, e mail).
**Organic Social**: the source is a known social site, or the medium is social, social-network, social-media, sm, social network or social media.
**Paid Social**: the source is a known social site and the medium contains cp, or is ppc, retargeting, or starts with paid.
**Direct**: no source is known. Clicks from some apps, including links shared in chats, often arrive with no referrer and end up here.
**Unassigned**: nothing matched, often because of a made-up medium.

blocks.text: UTM parameters

You control source and medium by adding **UTM parameters** to the end of links you share. Google says to always use utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign. utm_content separates different ads or posts, and utm_term is for paid keywords. Values are case-sensitive: Instagram and instagram become two separate rows, so use lowercase everywhere. Google's free Campaign URL Builder creates the link for you.

blocks.title: From tagged link to channel report
items: Tag link with UTMs
Visitor clicks and lands
GA4 stores source and medium
Key event recorded
Report by channel
blocks.caption: If the first step is skipped, the visit may be lost to Direct or Unassigned.

blocks.title: Worked example: tagging a Christmas campaign
blocks.context: For example, Funke sells celebration cakes in Ibadan through a website at example.com. In December she promotes a Christmas cake offer on WhatsApp broadcast, Instagram (bio and paid ads) and her newsletter.
steps: She agrees a campaign name: xmas_cakes_2026, all lowercase, words joined by underscores.
WhatsApp link: example.com/christmas?utm_source=whatsapp&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=xmas_cakes_2026
Instagram ad link: same page with utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=paid_social&utm_campaign=xmas_cakes_2026&utm_content=video_a, and video_b for the second ad.
Newsletter link: utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=xmas_cakes_2026.
She records every link in a sheet with date, channel, purpose and full URL, then tests each one on her phone and checks the GA4 Realtime report.
blocks.result: In January, GA4 can show Christmas orders by channel and even by ad video, instead of a large Direct row. The link sheet doubles as documentation for her report.

blocks.text: Settings to check on day one

items: In Admin, confirm the property time zone and currency match the business (for example, Africa/Lagos and Nigerian naira).

Set data retention to 14 months. Google's help centre explains that standard properties can choose 2 or 14 months, and that this setting limits explorations and funnel reports, not the standard reports.
Exclude internal traffic, such as your own office visits, if your setup allows it.
Mark the key events and test each one by completing the action yourself.
Link GA4 to Google Ads if the business advertises there, so ad costs and key events can be shared.

blocks.title: Privacy and consent
blocks.text: GA4 collects data about visitors' behaviour. Never send names, phone numbers or email addresses into GA4 events or URLs. Explain your tracking in the site's privacy notice and, where consent is required, ask before setting analytics cookies. Nigeria's data protection law is overseen by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, which recognises consent as one lawful basis for processing personal data.

takeaways: GA4 records events; the important ones are marked as key events.
Always set utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign, in lowercase.
Pick utm_medium values that match GA4 channel rules, such as email, social and paid_social.
Set data retention to 14 months and test every key event yourself.

activity.title: Build a UTM link sheet
steps: Choose one upcoming campaign for a real or practice business and give it a lowercase campaign name.
List every place a link will appear (bio, ads, WhatsApp, newsletter, partners).
Create a tagged link for each with the Campaign URL Builder, choosing source and medium from the table in this lesson.
Record each link in a sheet with date, channel, expected GA4 channel group and full URL.
Click each link on your phone and confirm the visit appears in GA4 Realtime with the right source and medium.
activity.evidence: The UTM link sheet and a screenshot of one tagged visit in GA4 Realtime.

lessons.title: Reconciling channel data: one sheet, one source of truth
objectives: Combine exports from ad platforms, GA4 and the order record into one long-format table
Explain five reasons platform, GA4 and order numbers disagree
Use payments received as the source of truth for orders and revenue
Report a channel's cost per purchase as an honest range plus a blended figure

blocks.text: No single tool sees all of a business's marketing. Meta Ads Manager sees Meta ads, Google Ads sees Google ads, GA4 sees website visits, and the payment platform or order book sees money. Your job is to bring these into one place, explain why they disagree, and decide which number to use for which decision.

blocks.name: organizing-data
blocks.alt: A person sorting data blocks into a neat table
blocks.caption: Reconciliation means lining up every source in one table before drawing conclusions.

blocks.text: A long-format master sheet

Build one Google Sheets or Excel table where each row is one channel (or campaign) for one period, and each column is one measure. This shape, called long format, is easy to filter, chart and connect to Looker Studio later. Typical columns: period, channel, campaign, spend, impressions, clicks, platform-reported purchases, platform-reported revenue, GA4 sessions, GA4 purchases, and a notes column for anything unusual.

Keep the order record on a separate tab: one row per order with date, amount, payment method (Paystack, bank transfer, Moniepoint POS, cash on delivery) and how the customer says they found you, if you ask. Remove customer names and phone numbers before sharing this tab with anyone outside the business.
Why the numbers disagree

items: **Different attribution rules and windows.** Each ad platform credits conversions within its own time window, and Meta can count view-through conversions, where a person only saw the ad.
**Double claiming.** Both Meta and Google may count the same order, because neither sees the other's touches.
**Tracking gaps.** Ad blockers, refused cookies, visitors switching from phone to laptop, and app browsers can stop GA4 or a pixel from seeing a purchase.
**Orders outside the website.** WhatsApp, Instagram DM and phone orders never reach GA4 unless you add them.
**Settings mismatches.** Different time zones, currencies or date ranges across tools shift results between days or months.

blocks.title: Platform claims vs money received
items: Platform-reported conversions
Orders and payments record
blocks.caption: Use platform numbers to optimise inside a platform and payment records to judge the whole budget.

blocks.title: Worked example: reconciling a month of kitchenware sales
blocks.context: For example, Ngozi sells kitchenware online from Port Harcourt. In November she spent 400,000 naira on Meta ads and 250,000 naira on Google Ads. Her Paystack dashboard and WhatsApp order list together show 86 paid orders worth 2,064,000 naira (average 24,000 naira).
steps: Platform claims: Meta reports 58 purchases worth 1,392,000 naira (ROAS 3.48); Google Ads reports 41 conversions worth 1,066,000 naira (ROAS about 4.26). Together: 99 purchases and 2,458,000 naira.
Reality check: 99 claimed purchases is 13 more than the 86 orders actually paid, so some orders were claimed twice or never happened as claimed.

GA4 (paid and organic last click) shows 82 website purchases: Paid Social 31, Paid Search 27, Organic Search 9, Direct 7, Email 5, Organic Social 3. Check: 31 + 27 + 9 + 7 + 5 + 3 = 82. The other 4 orders came only through WhatsApp.
Cost per purchase for Meta: 400,000 / 58 = about 6,897 naira by Meta's count, or 400,000 / 31 = about 12,903 naira by GA4 last click.
Cost per purchase for Google Ads: 250,000 / 41 = about 6,098 naira by Google's count, or 250,000 / 27 = about 9,259 naira by GA4 last click.
Blended figures from real money: MER = 2,064,000 / 650,000 = about 3.18; blended marketing cost per order = 650,000 / 86 = about 7,558 naira.
blocks.result: Ngozi's report states each channel's cost per purchase as a range (Meta 6,897 to 12,903 naira; Google 6,098 to 9,259 naira) and uses the blended 7,558 naira per order, from real payments, as the headline. Both channels look better in their own dashboards than in GA4, and Meta's gap is wider.

blocks.text: Checks before you trust the sheet

items: Match each platform's spend to its billing page or invoices for the same dates.
Confirm currency. If an ad account bills in US dollars, convert with one stated exchange rate and write the rate and its date in the notes.
Confirm every tool uses the same date range and, where possible, the same time zone.
Match orders and revenue to Paystack, bank or POS settlements, and remove refunds and cancelled orders.
Look for impossible values, such as more purchases than clicks, and find the cause before reporting.

blocks.title: Never add ROAS from two platforms
blocks.text: Adding or averaging Meta ROAS and Google ROAS counts double-claimed sales twice and gives a figure no one can check. For the whole budget, use MER and blended cost per order from real payments.
Keep a short **data log** tab: every export with its date, who pulled it, the date range and any filter used. When a client asks next quarter why a number changed, the log answers in seconds.

takeaways: Combine every source in one long-format table with a notes column.
Platform totals often exceed real orders because of double claiming and view-through counting.
Payments received are the source of truth for orders and revenue.
Report channel cost per purchase as a range, and lead with blended figures.

activity.title: Reconcile one month
steps: Export one month of spend and conversions from each ad platform a business uses (or use the worked example numbers as practice).
Export GA4 key events by session default channel group for the same dates.
Total real orders and revenue from the payment or order record, removing refunds.
Put all figures in one long-format table and calculate MER, blended cost per order and each channel's cost per purchase range.
Write three sentences explaining the biggest gap you found and its most likely cause.
activity.evidence: The reconciled sheet with a data log tab and the three-sentence explanation.

lessons.title: The monthly report: Looker Studio, insights and quality checks
objectives: Lay out a one-page marketing report in Looker Studio with scorecards, a trend and a channel table
Calculate percentage change and percentage-point change correctly
Write insights in the what, so what, now what format
Run a quality checklist and document caveats before sending

blocks.text: Your reconciled sheet now needs to become a report a busy owner reads in five minutes. Many analysts use **Looker Studio**, Google's free report and dashboard tool, because it connects directly to GA4, Google Ads and Google Sheets, updates when the data does, and can be shared as a view-only link that opens on a phone.

blocks.name: dashboard
blocks.alt: A dashboard with scorecards and charts
blocks.caption: One page, outcomes first, with every number traceable to the reconciled sheet.

blocks.text: A one-page layout that works

items: **Top row, scorecards**: revenue, orders, total marketing spend, MER and blended cost per order, each compared with the previous period.
**Middle, trend**: a line chart of weekly revenue and spend, so the reader sees timing, not just totals.
**Channel table**: one row per channel with spend, GA4 purchases, platform-reported purchases and cost per purchase range.
**Text box, insights**: three short insights with recommendations, written by you, not generated.
**Footer, caveats**: data sources, date range, attribution rule and known gaps.

blocks.text: Meta ads data does not have a free Google-made connector, so the usual low-cost route is to paste or import Meta exports into your Google Sheet, which Looker Studio then reads. Add a date range control so the reader can switch months, and use the scorecard's comparison setting for previous period.

blocks.title: Calculate ratios from totals
blocks.text: Create MER in Looker Studio as a calculated field, SUM(revenue) / SUM(spend), so it is computed from totals for whatever date range is selected. Averaging a column of weekly ratios gives a different, wrong answer whenever weeks differ in size.
Percent change versus percentage points

Percent change compares two values: (new - old) / old x 100. When the values are themselves rates, say "percentage points" for the simple difference. If conversion rate moves from 1.1% to 1.4%, it rose by **0.3 percentage points**, which is a **27% relative increase**. Mixing these up is one of the most common reporting errors, and it can make a small change sound huge or a big change sound small.

blocks.title: Worked example: three insights from Ngozi's November
blocks.context: For example, continuing Ngozi's kitchenware shop. October: 600,000 naira spend, 75 orders, 1,800,000 naira revenue, 6,450 sessions, 71 website purchases. November (from the reconciled sheet): 650,000 naira spend, 86 orders, 2,064,000 naira revenue, 5,860 sessions, 82 website purchases.
steps: Blended cost per order fell from 600,000 / 75 = 8,000 naira to about 7,558 naira, about 5.5% lower. MER rose from 3.0 to about 3.18.
Website conversion rate rose from 71 / 6,450 = 1.1% to 82 / 5,860 = 1.4%, up 0.3 percentage points, even though sessions fell.
Insight 1 (what): sales grew faster than spend. So what: each order cost less. Now what: keep total spend steady into December, a strong gifting month, and watch weekly cost per order.

Insight 2 (what): by GA4 last click, Google Ads cost about 9,259 naira per purchase against about 12,903 for Meta. So what: search appears more efficient, though Meta may be starting journeys that end in search. Now what: move 50,000 naira from Meta to search for December as a reversible test and judge it by blended cost per order.
Insight 3 (what): email brought 5 purchases. So what: too few to judge yet. Now what: send a weekly email in December and review again with more data.
blocks.result: The report leads with three numbers (revenue up 14.7%, cost per order down to about 7,558 naira, MER about 3.18), gives three insights each ending in an action with an owner, and states that channel costs are a range because platforms and GA4 disagree.

blocks.title: Quality checks before sending
items: Spend matches billing
Revenue matches payments
Same date range everywhere
Ratios built from totals
Caveats written down
blocks.caption: Five checks catch most errors that destroy trust in a report.

blocks.text: Compare like with like

Month-on-month comparisons can mislead when seasons differ. December includes Christmas gifting, and months containing Easter, Sallah or back-to-school periods behave differently for many Nigerian businesses. When you have a year of data, also compare with the same month last year. Mention calendar effects, public holidays and stock-outs in the caveats instead of letting the reader assume the marketing caused every change.

Finally, write the caveats in plain words: "Channel figures use GA4 paid and organic last click. Meta and Google Ads each report more purchases than GA4 because of their own attribution settings. Four WhatsApp-only orders have no channel." Two or three honest sentences protect your credibility far more than a confident number that later proves wrong.

takeaways: Lead the page with outcome scorecards compared to the previous period.
Build ratios from totals, never by averaging rows of ratios.
A move from 1.1% to 1.4% is 0.3 percentage points, or 27% relative.
Every insight needs what, so what and now what, plus honest caveats.

activity.title: Build and check a one-page report
steps: Connect your reconciled Google Sheet (or the GA4 demo data) to a new Looker Studio report.
Add five scorecards with previous-period comparison, one weekly trend chart and one channel table.
Create MER as a calculated field from summed revenue and summed spend.
Write three insights in what, so what, now what format, with numbers you have checked in a calculator.
Run the five-item quality checklist and add a caveats footer.
activity.evidence: A view-only link or PDF of the one-page report, plus the completed checklist.

quiz.q: Funke shares a link in a WhatsApp broadcast with utm_medium=broadcast. Where is the visit most likely to appear in GA4's default channel groups?
options: Unassigned or another wrong group, because broadcast matches no channel rule
quiz.explain: GA4 channel rules look for set medium values. A made-up medium such as broadcast does not match social or email rules, so use utm_medium=social instead.

quiz.q: Which three UTM parameters does Google say you should always use?
quiz.explain: Google's GA4 help says to always use utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign.

quiz.q: Meta reports 50 purchases, Google Ads reports 35, and the payment records show 70 paid orders. What is the best explanation?
options: The payment records must be wrong
Each platform counts under its own attribution rules, so some orders are claimed by both
Paystack only counts half of all orders
quiz.explain: Platforms do not see each other's touches and may count view-through conversions, so their totals can exceed real orders. Payments are the source of truth.

quiz.q: Total spend was 500,000 naira and payments show 80 orders. What is the blended marketing cost per order?
Conversion rate went from 2.0% to 2.5%. Which description is correct?
options: Up 0.5%, which is the same as 25%
Up 0.5 percentage points, a 25% relative increase

quiz.q: Ngozi's Meta ad account bills in US dollars and her report is in naira. What should she do?
options: Leave Meta spend in dollars next to naira figures
Convert using one stated exchange rate and record the rate and date in the notes
Use whichever rate makes Meta look best
quiz.explain: Mixed currencies break every ratio. Convert with one documented rate so the figures can be checked and repeated.

modules.title: Consulting, Pricing and Portfolio
modules.overview: You learn to run discovery and a measurement audit, price analytics work as a setup fee plus retainer with clear scope, and build portfolio proof and a 90-day plan to win your first paid analytics clients.

lessons.title: Discovery and the measurement audit
objectives: Run a discovery conversation that uncovers decisions, data sources and the people who will act
Request safe access to GA4, ad accounts and sales data without asking for passwords
Score a ten-point measurement audit and rank fixes by impact and effort
Apply basic data protection practice when handling a client's customer data

blocks.text: Before you build anything for a client, find out what she must decide, what data exists, and whether it can be trusted. This happens in two parts: a **discovery conversation** and a **measurement audit**. Together they tell you what to fix first, and they form the first paid piece of work in many analytics engagements.

blocks.name: interview
blocks.alt: Two people in a discussion across a table
blocks.caption: Discovery is mostly listening: decisions first, data second.

blocks.text: Discovery questions that matter

items: **Decisions**: What will you decide differently with better numbers? Budget size, channel split, which products to push, whether to hire an agency?
**Goals and margins**: What does a good month look like? Roughly what share of each sale is left after product and delivery costs?
**Channels**: Where do you market today (Meta, Google, TikTok, WhatsApp, email, influencers, markets and fairs) and roughly how much do you spend on each?
**Sales record**: Where is every order recorded? Website, Paystack, bank transfers, POS, WhatsApp, a notebook?
**Current reporting**: What do you look at now, how often, and what frustrates you about it?
**People**: Who will read the report, and who has the power to act on it?
**Format and rhythm**: Weekly WhatsApp summary, monthly PDF, live dashboard, or a monthly call?

blocks.text: Write the answers in a one-page discovery summary and send it back to the client to confirm. It prevents later arguments about what was agreed.
Getting access safely

Never ask for a client's passwords. Each platform lets the owner add you as a user with a limited role. In GA4 the owner adds your email in Admin under property access management; a Viewer or Analyst role is enough for reporting. In Meta, a business can give partner or people access to its ad account through Business settings. Google Ads also lets the owner invite you by email with a chosen access level. Ask for the lowest level that lets you do the work.

blocks.title: Protect customer data
blocks.text: Ask for sales exports with customer names, phone numbers and addresses removed, unless you truly need them. Store client files in a password-protected account, not on a shared family phone, and delete them when the engagement ends. Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023, enforced by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, gives people rights over their personal data, so treat every customer list as something you are trusted to protect.
The ten-point measurement audit

head: Check
Pass looks like
rows: Realtime report shows your test visit on all key pages
Purchase or lead key event fires once per action
Match the business and the ad accounts
Written rules, lowercase, used on every shared link
Google Ads linked to GA4; Meta exports available
7. Pixel or tags on ad platforms
Firing on the purchase or lead page, not double-firing
All channels, including WhatsApp and transfers, in one place
Platform spend equals invoices for a test month
Site explains tracking; no personal data in URLs or events

blocks.title: Worked example: an audit for an events caterer
blocks.context: For example, Kemi runs a catering company in Abuja. She spends on Instagram ads and Google search, takes enquiries through a website form and WhatsApp, and records confirmed jobs in a spreadsheet.
steps: Discovery shows her main decision: whether Google search is worth continuing, because enquiries feel low quality.

The audit finds 6 of 10 checks pass, a score of 60%. Failures: the form key event fires twice per submission, no UTM convention, WhatsApp enquiries are not recorded with a source, and there is no privacy notice.
The double-firing key event means Google Ads has been told it gets twice the real number of leads, so its cost per lead looks half what it is.

Fixes are ranked: fix the double-firing event and add a 'how did you hear about us' column for WhatsApp enquiries first (high impact, low effort), then the UTM convention, then the privacy notice with her web developer.
blocks.result: Kemi learns that her Google numbers were inflated before any report is built. The audit report, with the score and ranked fixes, becomes a paid deliverable and leads to a monthly reporting engagement once the fixes are in place.

blocks.title: Ranking audit fixes
items: High impact, low effort: do first
High impact, high effort: plan it
Low impact, low effort: batch together
Low impact, high effort: skip for now
blocks.caption: Sort every failed check by impact and effort so the client sees a clear order of work.

blocks.text: End the audit with a one-page summary: the score, the three most important problems in plain words, what each problem does to the numbers she sees today, and the fix order. Clients rarely understand tags and events, but they understand "your dashboard has been counting every enquiry twice".

takeaways: Discovery starts with decisions, margins and where every order is recorded.
Request user access with the lowest role needed; never ask for passwords.
A ten-point audit shows whether the data can be trusted before you report on it.
Rank fixes by impact and effort, and protect any customer data you receive.

activity.title: Audit one business
steps: Hold a 30-minute discovery conversation with a business owner (or role-play one) using the question list.
Write a one-page discovery summary and confirm it with the owner.
Run the ten-point audit on the business's website and accounts, or on your own practice site.
Score the audit and place every failed check in the impact and effort matrix.
Write the three most important problems in plain words with their fix order.
activity.evidence: The discovery summary and the scored audit with ranked fixes.

lessons.title: Pricing analytics work: setup fees, retainers and scope control
objectives: Estimate hours for a setup project and a monthly reporting retainer
Turn hours and your own target rate into a fee with contingency
Check a fee against the value of better decisions for the client
Write scope limits and a change-request rule into a proposal

blocks.text: Analytics work has a clear pattern: a lot of effort at the start (audit, fixes, tracking, building the report) and steady, smaller effort each month after. Pricing that matches this pattern is fairer to you and easier for the client to accept. The common structure is a **one-off setup fee** followed by a **monthly retainer**.

blocks.name: contract
blocks.alt: A person reviewing a signed contract
blocks.caption: A clear scope in the proposal protects both the client's budget and your time.

blocks.text: Step 1: estimate the hours

List every task and estimate hours honestly. Track your time on your first few projects so later estimates rest on evidence. Setup tasks usually include discovery, the audit, tracking fixes, the UTM convention and master sheet, the report build, quality checks and a handover call. Monthly tasks include pulling and checking data, analysis, writing insights and a review call.
Step 2: set your own rate

Your hourly rate is your decision. Start from what you need to earn per month, divide by the hours you can realistically bill (not every working hour is billable, because finding clients and learning take time), and adjust after speaking with peers and seeing what clients accept. The figures in this lesson are illustrative practice numbers, not market rates.

blocks.title: Worked example: pricing a setup and a retainer
blocks.context: For example, Zainab offers marketing analytics from Lagos and has set her own practice rate at 8,000 naira per hour (an approximate figure for this exercise). Her client spends about 650,000 naira a month on Meta and Google ads.
steps: Setup hours: discovery 3 + audit and fixes 8 + UTM convention and master sheet 4 + Looker Studio report 10 + QA and handover 3 = 28 hours.
Setup fee: 28 x 8,000 = 224,000 naira. She adds 15% contingency for surprises: 224,000 x 1.15 = 257,600, rounded to 260,000 naira.
Monthly hours: data pull and checks 3 + analysis and written insights 4 + review call 1 = 8 hours, so 8 x 8,000 = 64,000, rounded to 65,000 naira a month.

Value check: 65,000 naira is 10% of the client's 650,000 naira monthly ad spend. If her reports help the client cut wasted spend or lower cost per order by even 10%, that alone is worth about 65,000 naira a month.
Payment terms: 50% of the setup fee (130,000 naira) before work starts, the rest on handover; retainer paid at the start of each month.
blocks.result: The proposal shows a 260,000 naira setup and a 65,000 naira monthly retainer, explains the hours behind them, and links the fee to the money the client could save. The client can see exactly what she pays for.

blocks.title: Setup project vs monthly retainer
items: Setup project
Monthly retainer
blocks.caption: Separating the two makes the large first effort visible and keeps the monthly fee predictable.

blocks.text: Step 3: write the scope

items: **Data sources included**: for example, GA4, Google Ads, Meta Ads and the payment record. Any new source is extra.
**Deliverables and dates**: one report by the 5th working day of each month and one 45-minute call.
**Revisions**: up to two rounds of changes on the report design during setup.
**Exclusions**: running ads, designing content and fixing the website code are not included.
**Client duties**: give access within an agreed number of days and share the sales record each month.
**Change requests**: new analysis outside scope is quoted in writing before work starts.

blocks.title: Scope creep in analytics
blocks.text: "Can you just quickly check why sales dropped last Tuesday?" is how unpaid hours begin. Answer kindly, estimate the hours, and offer to add it as a small paid task or to fold it into next month's report. Agree before you start, in writing, even on WhatsApp.
A stand-alone audit as the first sale

Many owners hesitate to commit to a monthly fee before they trust you. A fixed-price measurement audit, using the ten-point checklist from the previous lesson plus a short written summary, is an easier first yes. Price it from your hours in the same way, keep it small enough to finish in a week or two, and end it with a clear proposal for the fixes and the retainer. If the client does not continue, she still owns a useful document, and you have a case study.

Review every retainer after three months. Compare the hours you actually spent with the hours you priced. If you are regularly over, either the scope has grown or your estimate was low; raise it with the client using your time log as evidence, rather than quietly absorbing the extra work.
Bundling with other services

If you also run ads or social media for the client, you can bundle reporting into that fee. Be careful: when you report on campaigns you manage, the client may doubt your neutrality. State your attribution rules, show payment-based blended figures, and include bad news as clearly as good news. Some analysts prefer to stay independent so their reports carry more weight.

takeaways: Price analytics as a setup fee plus a monthly retainer.
Fee = honest hours x your own rate, plus contingency, then check it against client value.
Write data sources, deliverables, revisions, exclusions and a change-request rule into scope.
Take a deposit before setup work starts.

activity.title: Price a real or practice client
steps: Choose a client type and list every setup and monthly task.
Estimate hours for each task and total them.
Set your own hourly rate from your income needs and billable hours, and calculate both fees with contingency.
Check the monthly fee as a share of the client's ad spend and write one sentence on its value.
Write a one-page proposal with scope, exclusions, payment terms and a change-request rule.
activity.evidence: The pricing calculation sheet and the one-page proposal.

lessons.title: Market opportunities, portfolio proof and a 90-day plan
objectives: Identify client types in Nigeria and abroad that need marketing analytics
Build a portfolio case study from practice data or the GA4 demo account
Name a free, recognised credential for GA4 skills
Write a 90-day plan with weekly targets and a simple conversion funnel

blocks.text: Marketing analytics is useful anywhere a business pays for marketing and wants to know if it works. It is also remote-friendly: the data lives in cloud tools, so you can serve a client in another state or another country from your phone and laptop. Many analysts start by adding reporting to other digital marketing skills, then grow it into a stand-alone service.

blocks.name: portfolio-website
blocks.alt: A person presenting work samples on a portfolio website
blocks.caption: Proof of real analysis, clearly labelled, persuades clients more than any list of skills.

blocks.text: Who needs this work

items: **Online shops and Instagram sellers** spending on Meta or Google ads and unsure what is paying back.
**Service businesses** such as caterers, schools, clinics, salons and real estate firms that buy leads and need cost per qualified lead.
**Digital marketing agencies and freelancers** who run campaigns but need help with tracking setups and client reports.
**NGOs and social enterprises** that run awareness or recruitment campaigns and report to funders.
**International clients** found through freelance marketplaces or referrals, who often expect GA4 and Looker Studio skills.

blocks.text: Practice data you can use legally

You do not need a client to start. Google provides a free **GA4 demo account** that anyone with a Google account can open with a Viewer role. According to Google's help centre it contains two properties, the **Google Merchandise Store**, an ecommerce site, and **Flood-It!**, a mobile game, with real but obfuscated data. You can explore channels, key events and purchases, and connect it to Looker Studio for practice reports. You can also build a realistic practice dataset in Google Sheets, as long as you label it clearly as practice data.

blocks.title: A free credential
blocks.text: Google offers a free Google Analytics Certification through its Skillshop learning platform. It shows employers and clients that you know GA4. Check the current requirements on Skillshop before you start, and add the certificate to your portfolio once earned.
A portfolio case study that persuades

items: **Situation**: who the business is (or that it is practice data) and the decision it faced.
**What you did**: audit score, tracking fixes, reconciliation, report built.
**What you found**: one or two insights with checked numbers, such as a channel cost per purchase range.
**What changed**: the action taken and the result, or the planned test if results are not in yet.
**Artefacts**: a screenshot of the report with private data blurred, and the measurement plan.

blocks.text: Always ask permission before showing a client's work, blur names and figures if asked, and never claim a result you cannot show. A practice case study, honestly labelled, is better than an inflated real one.

blocks.title: Your 90 days
items: Weeks 1-2: certificate and demo
Weeks 3-4: case study live
Weeks 5-8: 5 contacts weekly
Weeks 9-12: audits and proposals
Day 90: review the numbers
blocks.caption: Each block produces something visible, so progress can be measured like any campaign.

blocks.title: Worked example: a 90-day plan with weekly numbers
blocks.context: For example, Chidinma already manages social media for two clients in Enugu and wants paid analytics work by the end of the quarter. Her conversion guesses are her own planning assumptions, to be replaced by real figures as she goes.
steps: Weeks 1 to 4: earn the Google Analytics Certification, build a Looker Studio report on the GA4 demo account, and write one practice case study.
Weeks 5 to 12: contact 5 suitable businesses per week with a short message offering a measurement audit. That is 5 x 12 = 60 contacts.
If 1 in 10 contacts books a discovery call, she gets 60 x 0.1 = 6 calls.
If 1 in 3 calls becomes a paid audit, she wins 6 / 3 = 2 clients by day 90.
Every Friday she logs contacts, calls and proposals in a sheet, exactly like a marketing funnel report.
blocks.result: Chidinma's plan has clear weekly activity targets and an expected outcome of two paid audits. On day 90 she compares her real rates with her guesses and adjusts the next quarter, using the same analytics habits she sells.

blocks.text: Reaching the first clients

Your first outreach message should be short and specific: who you are, one problem you noticed (for example, their ads link to a page with no tracking, or their bio link has no UTM tags), and a small offer such as a fixed-price audit. Send it where the owner actually reads messages, which for many Nigerian businesses is WhatsApp or Instagram direct messages. Never send bulk unsolicited messages, and stop if someone asks you to.

For remote and international clients, agree the time zone for calls and deadlines, the currency of your fee and how you will be paid before work starts. Put these terms in the proposal so there is no confusion when the first invoice is due.

Your capstone for this course brings everything together: a measurement plan, a reconciled dataset, a one-page report with insights, and a pricing proposal with this 90-day plan. Treat it as the first item in your portfolio.

takeaways: Shops, service firms, agencies, NGOs and remote clients all need marketing analytics.
The GA4 demo account and labelled practice data let you build proof before your first client.
A case study shows situation, actions, findings and results, with permission and honesty.
Run your own 90-day plan as a funnel with weekly targets and review the real rates.

activity.title: Write your 90-day plan
steps: Choose one client type from the lesson list and write why you suit them.
Open the GA4 demo account and note three findings from the Google Merchandise Store channels report.
Draft one portfolio case study using the five-part structure.
Set weekly activity targets for contacts, calls and proposals, and calculate the expected clients.
Create a tracking sheet to log your weekly numbers.
activity.evidence: The 90-day plan, the draft case study and the weekly tracking sheet.

quiz.q: A client offers to send you her Meta and Google passwords so you can pull reports. What should you do?
options: Accept but change the passwords afterwards
Decline and ask her to add you as a user with a limited role on each platform
Ask her to screenshot the reports every month instead
quiz.explain: Each platform supports user access with roles. Ask for the lowest role you need and never hold a client's passwords.

quiz.q: During an audit you find the lead key event fires twice per form submission. What does this do to Google Ads cost per lead?
options: It makes cost per lead look about half its true value
It doubles the real cost per lead
It has no effect on cost per lead
quiz.explain: Twice the leads are counted for the same spend, so cost per lead appears roughly halved, making the campaign look better than it is.

quiz.q: Zainab estimates 20 setup hours at her rate of 10,000 naira and adds 15% contingency. What is the setup fee before rounding?
A retainer client asks you to 'quickly' analyse a new TikTok campaign not in your scope. What is the best response?
options: Do it quietly to keep the client happy
Estimate the hours and offer it as a quoted change request or add it to next month's scope, agreed in writing
Drop another part of the report without telling her
quiz.explain: Scope control means extra work is estimated and agreed before you start. This protects your time and keeps trust.

quiz.q: You have no clients yet. What is the most honest way to show GA4 skill in your portfolio?
options: Describe invented results for a made-up company as if real
Build a report from the GA4 demo account or labelled practice data
Copy a published case study from an agency
Only list the tools you know
quiz.explain: The GA4 demo account and clearly labelled practice data show real skill without false claims.

quiz.q: Chidinma plans 4 contacts a week for 10 weeks, expects 1 in 8 to book a call, and 1 in 2 calls to become a client. How many clients does she expect?
quiz.explain: 4 x 10 = 40 contacts; 40 / 8 = 5 calls; 5 / 2 = 2.5 clients, so about 2 or 3.

finalQuiz.q: A client's report shows impressions, likes and posts made. Which number should lead a budget report instead?
options: Marketing cost per order from real payments
finalQuiz.explain: Owners decide budgets on outcomes. Cost per order from real payments ties spend directly to sales.

finalQuiz.q: Why should you not add Meta ROAS and Google ROAS together to judge the whole budget?
options: Each platform may claim the same sale, so adding counts some sales twice
finalQuiz.explain: Platforms each credit conversions under their own rules. MER from total revenue and total spend avoids double counting.

finalQuiz.q: A shop has 8,000 sessions, 2% conversion and an average order value of 12,500 naira. What is revenue?
An order worth 90,000 naira had three touches. Under linear attribution, how much does each touch get?
finalQuiz.explain: Linear shares credit equally: 90,000 / 3 = 30,000 naira each.

finalQuiz.q: Ads reached 3,000 people and 180 bought; a held-out group of 3,000 had 150 purchases. Spend was 120,000 naira. What is the cost per incremental purchase?
Half of a team tags links with utm_source=Instagram and half with utm_source=instagram. What happens in GA4?
options: They appear as two separate sources, splitting the data
finalQuiz.explain: UTM values are case-sensitive, so use lowercase everywhere to avoid fragmented data.

finalQuiz.q: A newsletter link uses utm_source=newsletter and utm_medium=email. Which default channel group should it appear in?
finalQuiz.explain: GA4's Email channel rule matches a source or medium of email.

finalQuiz.q: Meta, Google Ads, GA4 and Paystack all report different purchase totals. Which should be the headline source for orders and revenue?
finalQuiz.explain: Real payments count each sale once and include orders outside the website, so they are the source of truth.

finalQuiz.q: A conversion rate rises from 3% to 4%. How should the report describe it?
finalQuiz.explain: 4 - 3 = 1 percentage point; 1 / 3 is about a 33% relative increase.

finalQuiz.q: Week 1: spend 100,000, revenue 500,000. Week 2: spend 300,000, revenue 600,000. What is the correct MER for the two weeks?
finalQuiz.explain: Use totals: 1,100,000 / 400,000 = 2.75. Averaging the weekly ratios (5.0 and 2.0) wrongly gives 3.5.

finalQuiz.q: Your audit finds GA4 data retention set to 2 months. Why change it to 14 months?
options: It lets explorations and funnel reports look back over longer periods
finalQuiz.explain: Google says retention limits explorations and funnel reports; 14 months allows year-on-year analysis there.

finalQuiz.q: A retainer covers 6 hours a month at your rate of 9,000 naira. What is the monthly fee before rounding?

capstone.title: Marketing Analytics Dashboard, Insight Report and Analytics Offer
capstone.brief: Using real business data (with permission) or clearly labelled practice data, you produce a measurement plan, a reconciled dataset, a one-page Looker Studio report with three actionable insights and caveats, and a priced proposal with a 90-day plan for offering analytics work to one client type.
steps: Write a one-page measurement plan with objective, primary KPI, driver formulas, baselines, targets and a KPI tree.
Create a UTM link sheet for one campaign and confirm at least one tagged visit in GA4 (your own site or a test page).
Build a long-format master sheet reconciling ad platform figures, GA4 key events and payment records, with a data log.
Calculate MER, blended cost per order and a cost per purchase range for each paid channel, checking every sum.
Build a one-page Looker Studio report with scorecards, a trend, a channel table, three insights and a caveats footer.
Write a pricing proposal (setup and retainer) with scope limits, plus a 90-day plan with weekly targets.
evidence: UTM link sheet and GA4 screenshot
Reconciled master sheet with data log
Looker Studio report link or PDF
Three insights in what, so what, now what format
